correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the entire finite domain: [10 choose 2]_2=174251, generated GL4(F2) with adjacent coordinate transpositions and an elementary transvection, enumerated all pencils and traversed their 54 actual orbits; size sum 174251. For each of 54 orbit seeds, an independently implemented SymPy characteristic-two Gröbner calculation used both defining quadrics and all six 2x2 Jacobian minors on each of four projective affine charts; precisely eight seeds have unit ideals on every chart, totaling 40320 smooth pencils with sizes 2520 twice, 5040 five times and 10080 once. Complete intersection adjunction gives degree four and genus one; over F2 all smooth elliptic curves have rational points. Independent direct 15-point evaluations returned every mask, N=1,2,2,3,4,4,4,5, and each sorted 5/7/9 quadric-point profile. Local power-series solution through order three at every rational point verified the 4P osculating-plane counts 1,0,2,1,0,4,0,1; explicit GF2 Groebner elimination for (20,609), x0=0, x2=1 gave (x1+x3^3+x3^2,x3^4) with no points at x2=0, length four. Direct enumeration of all 15 planes verified coplanarity unique to (20,842) among N=4. All seven-/five-/nine-point member types were separately checked by exact F2 gradients and rational counts. The exact finite algorithm is a proof of this finite classification; neither finite experiments nor logs are invoked as infinite-field proofs.
residual_risks: Enumeration is proved only over the fixed field F2; no inference for arbitrary finite or infinite fields.

evidence: For N=4, E(F2) is Z/4, Pic^4 classes modulo +/- have orbits {0},{2},{1,3}. A rational hyperplane with divisor 4P exists when L=O(4P); all-four-rational-points coplanarity corresponds to L=O(sum E(F2))=class 2. Thus 4P/coplanarity separation itself follows standard divisor arithmetic.
The eight smooth sizes (two 2520, five 5040 and one 10080) sum to 40320, and numerical eight and class multiplicities can be derived from the known E(F2) groups plus stabilizer theory.

Neither Husemöller’s five unpolarized class table nor Krishna’s characteristic-zero j-fiber orbit theorem gives the exact per-embedding three-quadric (5,7,9) spectra and binary representative masks. Independent finite-field algebra is needed for those remaining data.

evidence: A smooth (2,2) complete intersection in P3 is an elliptic normal quartic (genus one and degree-four line bundle); its defining space of quadrics is a unique 2-plane. Conversely a genus-one curve with a very ample degree-four line bundle embeds by four sections as such an intersection.
Husemöller §6 lists five F2 elliptic curves with groups of orders 1,2,3,4,5 (the order-four group is Z/4).

Pic^4(E)(F2) is an E(F2)-torsor; translation by T changes degree-four class by 4T, and origin-fixing inversion identifies classes R and -R. Hence 1,2,1,3,1 degree-four polarization orbits for the five group sizes; the count of eight projective types alone is classically deducible.

originality.rationale: The result is mathematically equivalent to a degree-four polarization classification of elliptic curves over F2. The eight-orbit headline and contact/coplanarity distinction are substantially classically implied by Husemöller’s five curve classes and Picard/automorphism facts; these are not counted as novel by themselves. However the actual final claim contains a complete per-embedding joint profile of all three rational defining quadrics (split, nonsplit, cone), explicit binary masks, smooth pencil counts and finite orbit multiplicities. Searches and full relevant source passages found no directly covering table; this incremental exact census is accepted best of knowledge with explicit unindexed-prior-table risk.
residual_risks: The eight polarized class count, many orbit sizes and rational osculation/coplanarity strata already follow classical elliptic-curve/Picard group theory; only the complete joint quadric-profile table and explicit attached representatives support incremental originality.
A previously tabulated characteristic-two pencil classification in unindexed finite-geometry literature could cover these additional profiles.
The Fisher invariant paper and some other broader primary works were not read in full; absence from examined parts or abstracts is not whole-paper noncoverage.

value.rationale: A smooth degree-four elliptic normal curve and its unique 2D defining space of quadrics are canonical basic embedded genus-one models. Over the smallest field, the finite classification is a natural complete moduli question rather than a parameter slice. The joint arithmetic type of its THREE rational pencil quadrics (nonsplit 5-point, singular cone 7-point, split 9-point) is an informative embedded invariant not implied by the unpolarized point-count classification and not seen as an exact preexisting table. The per-type multiplicities, rational contact and coplanarity distinguish naturally polarized models. Eight-orbit counts and some contact features follow classical Picard theory, so they do not alone justify value; the complete exact binary quadric-profile atlas and reproducible finite geometric smoothness certificates provide the nontrivial remaining standalone fact, with meaningful potential use as small-field test cases in arithmetic geometry and finite projective geometry.
residual_risks: No general-field theorem or downstream consequence is claimed; the value is that of a complete exact small-field embedded table.
If a matching joint table exists already, originality and therefore asserted value would need reevaluation.

limitations: Scientific classification is exact only for two-dimensional quadratic systems over F2 in P3, smooth scheme-theoretic complete intersections; none of the singular systems or extensions to other fields are classified.

Some numerical headline counts and order-four contact/coplanarity pattern are consequences of classical F2 elliptic curve and Pic4 geometry; only the complete joint triple-quadric profile is treated as incremental novelty.
Priority is best-of-knowledge, not exhaustive; unindexed finite-geometry tables or unseen primary full texts might cover the exact table.
